title: Network structure of social–emotional skills and well‐being from a PYD perspective: A cross‐age comparison
abstract: Abstract Positive youth development (PYD) frameworks emphasize that young people thrive when they develop social–emotional skills that support adaptive functioning and well‐being. Although a growing body of research has examined social–emotional skills, less is known about how they are interconnected with different dimensions of well‐being and whether these patterns differ across age cohorts. To address these gaps, this study examined the joint structure of social–emotional skills and well‐being from a PYD perspective. Data were drawn from the OECD Survey on Social and Emotional Skills (SSES), comprising 60,985 students from 10 cities across nine participating countries. Network analysis was used to map the interconnections between social–emotional skills and well‐being separately among 10‐year‐old children and 15‐year‐old adolescents, and to compare the network structures of the two age cohorts. Optimism and cooperation were the most central skills in both cohorts, whereas optimism and life satisfaction showed the strongest cross‐community associations. The overall network structure differed between the two cohorts, with additional cohort differences observed for several specific centrality indices and connections between social–emotional skills and well‐being. These findings deepen understanding of how social–emotional skills and well‐being are jointly organized and highlight the importance of adopting a developmentally sensitive approach to PYD research and practice.
